pains: I buy 'fresh' coffee at the store and have no idea when it was actually roasted. It could've been sitting there for months.
My coffee tastes flat by the second week and I don't know if it's me or the beans.
Every bag has a vague 'premium blend' label. I can't tell where it's from or who grew it.
I've spent real money on fancy beans and still got a bitter, muddy cup.
I'm tired of running out of coffee and ending up with whatever's left on the shelf at the grocery store.
desires: I want to open a bag and actually smell something fresh, not stale cardboard.
I want to know where my coffee comes from, like the actual origin and not just a country on the label.
I want my morning brew to feel like a small ritual I look forward to, not just caffeine.
I want to grind whole beans myself and taste the difference.
I want good coffee to just show up so I stop thinking about it.
I want to support roasters who actually care about what they're making.
objections: Subscriptions scare me. What if I end up with too much coffee piling up?
Is it really that different from what I already buy, or is it just a nicer bag?
Small batch sounds nice but it's probably a marketing word.
I only have a basic setup at home. Is this going to be too fussy for me?
I'm not sure I want to commit to one origin. What if I don't like how it tastes?
I've seen a hundred coffee ads like this. Why should I trust this one?
proof_points: Every bag is whole beans, so you grind right before you brew.
The roast date is printed on every bag, so you can see exactly when it was roasted.
It's single-origin, so the beans come from one place and not a mystery blend.
It comes as a monthly subscription box, so a new bag shows up on a regular rhythm.
